'primary' : null,\n          repository.lastBranch ? `branch ${repository.lastBranch}` : null,\n          repository.lastHead ? `HEAD ${repository.lastHead.slice(0, 8)}` : null,\n        ].filter((part): part is string => part !== null);\n        return relative.join(' · ');\n      }),\n    ),\n  );\n\n  out.push(heading(2, 'Constraints'));\n  out.push(\n    list(\n      snapshot.constraints.map((constraint) => {\n        const scope = constraint.subsystem ? ` _(${constraint.subsystem})_` : '';\n        const state = constraint.active ? '' : ' **[inactive]**';\n        return `**${constraint.severity}** — ${constraint.statement}${scope}${state} \\`${constraint.id}\\``;\n      }),\n    ),\n  );\n\n  out.push(heading(2, 'Decisions'));\n  out.push(\n    list(\n      snapshot.decisions.map((decision) => {\n        const parts = [`${decision.statement} \\`${decision.id}\\``];\n        if (decision.rationale) parts.push(`  - why: ${decision.rationale}`);\n        if (decision.alternatives.length > 0) parts.push(`  - considered: ${decision.alternatives.join('; ')}`);\n        if (decision.subsystem) parts.push(`  - subsystem: ${decision.subsystem}`);\n        if (decision.status === 'superseded') parts.push(`  - superseded by ${decision.supersededBy ?? 'unknown'}`);\n        return parts.join('\\n');\n      }),\n    ),\n  );\n\n  out.push(heading(2, 'Known bugs'));\n  out.push(\n    list(\n      snapshot.bugs.map((bug) => {\n        const parts = [`**${bug.severity}** / ${bug.status} — ${bug.title} \\`${bug.id}\\``];\n        if (bug.observed) parts.push(`  - observed: ${bug.observed}`);\n        if (bug.expected) parts.push(`  - expected: ${bug.expected}`);\n        if (bug.reproduction) parts.push(`  - reproduction: ${bug.reproduction}`);\n        if (bug.evidence.length > 0) parts.push(`  - evidence: ${bug.evidence.join('; ')}`);\n        if (bug.files.length > 0) parts.push(`  - files: ${bug.files.join(', ')}`);\n        return parts.join('\\n');\n      }),\n    ),\n  );\n\n  out.push(heading(2, 'Findings'));\n  out.push(\n    list(\n      snapshot.findings.map((finding) => {\n        const parts = [`**${finding.confidence}** — ${finding.statement} \\`${finding.id}\\``];\n        if (finding.symbols.length > 0) parts.push(`  - symbols: ${finding.symbols.join(', ')}`);\n        if (finding.files.length > 0) parts.push(`  - files: ${finding.files.join(', ')}`);\n        if (finding.evidence.length > 0) parts.push(`  - evidence: ${finding.evidence.join('; ')}`);\n        parts.push(`  - meaning: ${CONFIDENCE_CRITERIA[finding.confidence]}`);\n        return parts.join('\\n');\n      }),\n    ),\n  );\n\n  out.push(heading(2, 'Tasks'));\n  out.push(\n    list(\n      snapshot.tasks.map((task) => {\n        const parts = [`**${task.priority}** / ${task.status} — ${task.title} \\`${task.id}\\``];\n        if (task.subsystem) parts.push(`  - subsystem: ${task.subsystem}`);\n        if (task.affectedFiles.length > 0) parts.push(`  - files: ${task.affectedFiles.join(', ')}`);\n        parts.push(`  - verification: ${task.verificationStatus}`);\n        if (task.verificationRequirements.length > 0) {\n          parts.push(`  - requirements: ${task.verificationRequirements.join('; ')}`);\n        }\n        if (task.blockers.length > 0) parts.push(`  - blockers: ${task.blockers.join('; ')}`);\n        if (task.dependencies.length > 0) parts.push(`  - depends on: ${task.dependencies.join(', ')}`);\n        return parts.join('\\n');\n      }),\n    ),\n  );\n\n  out.push(heading(2, 'Verification history'));\n  out.push(\n    list(\n      snapshot.verifications.map((verification) => {\n        const command = verification.command ? ` (\\`${verification.command}\\`)` : '';\n        const task = verification.taskId ? ` for ${verification.taskId}` : '';\n        const evidence = verification.evidence.length > 0 ? ` — ${verification.evidence.join('; ')}` : '';\n        return `${verification.result}: ${verification.method}${command}${task} · ${verification.createdAt} \\`${verification.id}\\`${evidence}`;\n      }),\n    ),\n  );\n\n  out.push(heading(2, 'Handoffs'));\n  out.push(\n    list(\n      snapshot.handoffs.map((handoff) => {\n        const parts = [`${handoff.summary} \\`${handoff.id}\\` · ${handoff.createdAt}`];\n        if (handoff.workCompleted) parts.push(`  - completed: ${handoff.workCompleted}`);\n        if (handoff.workAttempted) parts.push(`  - attempted: ${handoff.workAttempted}`);\n        if (handoff.failures.length > 0) parts.push(`  - failures: ${handoff.failures.join('; ')}`);\n        if (handoff.blockers.length > 0) parts.push(`  - blockers: ${handoff.blockers.join('; ')}`);\n        if (handoff.unresolved.length > 0) parts.push(`  - unresolved: ${handoff.unresolved.join('; ')}`);\n        if (handoff.followUp.length > 0) parts.push(`  - follow-up: ${handoff.followUp.join('; ')}`);\n        if (handoff.head) parts.push(`  - head: ${handoff.head}`);\n        return parts.join('\\n');\n      }),\n    ),\n  );\n\n  return `${out.join('\\n\\n')}\\n`;\n}\n",

'';\n    if (literal) {\n      positionals.push(token);\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (token === '--') {\n      literal = true;\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (token.startsWith('--') || (token.startsWith('-') && token.length > 1 && !/^-\\d/.test(token))) {\n      const body = token.startsWith('--') ? token.slice(2) : token.slice(1);\n      const eq = body.indexOf('=');\n      const rawName = eq === -1 ? body : body.slice(0, eq);\n      const name = canonical(rawName, specs);\n      if (!name) return { ok: false, error: `unknown flag --${rawName}` };\n\n      if (eq !== -1) {\n        assign(name, body.slice(eq + 1));\n        continue;\n      }\n      if (isBoolean(name, specs)) {\n        assign(name, true);\n        continue;\n      }\n      const next = argv[index + 1];\n      if (next === undefined) return { ok: false, error: `flag --${rawName} requires a value` };\n      assign(name, next);\n      index += 1;\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    positionals.push(token);\n  }\n\n  return { ok: true, parsed: { positionals, flags } };\n}\n\n/** Single string value for a flag, or undefined. */\nexport function flagString(parsed: ParsedArgs, name: string): string | undefined {\n  const value = parsed.flags.get(name);\n  if (value === undefined) return undefined;\n  if (Array.isArray(value)) {\n    const last = value[value.length - 1];\n    return typeof last === 'string' ? last : undefined;\n  }\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : undefined;\n}\n\n/** All values for a repeatable flag. */\nexport function flagList(parsed: ParsedArgs, name: string): string[] {\n  const value = parsed.flags.get(name);\n  if (value === undefined) return [];\n  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.filter((item): item is string => typeof item === 'string');\n  return typeof value === 'string' ? 125: function parseLog(stdout: string): ParsedLog {

131:     const trimmed = record.replace(/^\n+/, '');
132:     if (!trimmed) continue;
133:     const [header = '', ...fileLines] = trimmed.split('\n');
134:     const [hash = '', shortHash = '', author = '', date = '', ...subjectParts] = header.split(FIELD_SEPARATOR);
135:     if (!hash) continue;
136:     const files = fileLines
137:       .map((line) => line.trim())
138:       .filter((line) => line.length > 0)
139:       .slice(0, MAX_FILES_PER_COMMIT);
140:     commits.push({
141:       hash,
142:       shortHash: shortHash || hash.slice(0, 7),
143:       author,
144:       date,
145:       subject: subjectParts.join(FIELD_SEPARATOR),
146:       files,
147:     });
148:     for (const file of files) {
149:       if (seenFiles.has(file) || recentFiles.length >= MAX_RECENT_FILES) continue;
150:       seenFiles.add(file);
151:       recentFiles.push(file);
152:     }
153:   }
154:   return { commits, recentFiles };
155: }

426: /**
427:  * Render the brief as text, trimming to fit the token budget.
428:  *
429:  * Trimming order is deterministic: the lowest-priority section loses its last
430:  * item, then the next, until the budget is met; a section that loses all its
431:  * items is removed entirely. Priority-0 sections are never dropped — the brief
432:  * will slightly exceed the budget rather than hide a critical constraint, the
433:  * verification plan, or the next action.
434:  */
435: export function renderBrief(brief: Brief, options: RenderOptions = {}): string {
436:   const budget = options.maxTokens ?? defaultMaxTokens(brief);
437:   let sections = buildSections(brief);
438: 
439:   if (approxTokens(renderSections(sections)) <= budget) return `${renderSections(sections)}\n`;
440: 
441:   const trimmable = sections
442:     .filter((section) => section.priority > 0 && section.items.length > 0)
443:     .sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority || a.title.localeCompare(b.title));
444: 
445:   for (const section of trimmable) {
446:     while (section.items.length > 0 && approxTokens(renderSections(sections)) > budget) {
447:       section.items.pop();
448:     }
449:     if (approxTokens(renderSections(sections)) <= budget) break;
450:   }
451: 
452:   // Still over budget: drop whole low-priority sections, headings included.
453:   for (const section of [...sections].filter((s) => s.priority > 0).sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority)) {
454:     if (approxTokens(renderSections(sections)) <= budget) break;
455:     sections = sections.filter((candidate) => candidate !== section);
456:   }
457: 
458:   return `${renderSections(sections)}\n`;
459: }

98: /** Classify the task type from its wording. First strong match wins. */
99: export function classifyTaskType(task: string): { type: TaskType; confidence: InferenceConfidence } {
100:   const scores = new Map<TaskType, number>();
101:   for (const { type, patterns } of TYPE_PATTERNS) {
102:     let score = 0;
103:     for (const pattern of patterns) {
104:       const matches = task.match(new RegExp(pattern.source, 'gi'));
105:       if (matches) score += matches.length;
106:     }
107:     if (score > 0) scores.set(type, score);
108:   }
109:   const ranked = [...scores.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]);
110:   const best = ranked[0];
111:   if (!best) return { type: 'unknown', confidence: 'low' };
112:   const runnerUp = ranked[1];
113:   const confidence: InferenceConfidence = best[1] >= 3 && (!runnerUp || best[1] > runnerUp[1]) ? 'high' : best[1] >= 2 ? 'medium' : 'low';
114:   return { type: best[0], confidence };
115: }
116: 
117: export function isReverseEngineeringTask(task: string, projectPhase: string | null | undefined): boolean {
118:   if (projectPhase && /reverse|re\b|disassembl|decompil|binary|runtime validation|symbol/i.test(projectPhase)) return true;
119:   return RE_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(task));
120: }

126:  * for the project, so inference improves as the project's memory grows.
127:  */

132: ): { subsystems: string[]; confidence: InferenceConfidence } {
133:   const termSet = new Set(taskTerms);
134:   const scored: Array<{ name: string; score: number }> = [];
135: 
136:   for (const subsystem of knownSubsystems) {
137:     const parts = [...new Set([...splitWords(subsystem).map(normalizeTerm), ...pathTokens(subsystem)])].filter(
138:       (part) => part.length >= 3,
139:     );
140:     if (parts.length === 0) continue;
141:     let score = 0;
142:     // Whole-name match on a multi-word name is the strongest signal.
143:     if (task.toLowerCase().includes(subsystem.toLowerCase().replace(/[-_]+/g, ' '))) score += 1.5;
144:     else if (task.toLowerCase().includes(subsystem.toLowerCase())) score += 1.4;
145:     for (const part of parts) {
146:       if (termSet.has(part)) score += 1;
147:       else if ([...termSet].some((term) => term.startsWith(part) || part.startsWith(term))) score += 0.4;
148:     }
149:     // Require at least a partial word overlap; a single shared stop-ish word is noise.
150:     const normalisedScore = score / Math.sqrt(parts.length);
151:     if (normalisedScore >= 0.75) scored.push({ name: subsystem, score: normalisedScore });
152:   }
153: 
154:   scored.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score || a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
155:   const subsystems = scored.slice(0, 3).map((entry) => entry.name);
156:   const confidence: InferenceConfidence =
157:     subsystems.length === 0 ? 'low' : (scored[0]?.score ?? 0) >= 1.6 ? 'high' : 'medium';
158:   return { subsystems, confidence };
159: }

161: /** Directory- or filename-derived components, used when the caller lists files. */
162: function componentsFromFiles(files: readonly string[]): string[] {
163:   const out: string[] = [];
164:   for (const file of files) {
165:     const segments = file.replace(/\\/g, '/').split('/').filter(Boolean);
166:     const directory = segments.length > 1 ? segments[segments.length - 2] : undefined;
167:     const name = segments[segments.length - 1] ?? file;
168:     const label = directory ? `${name} (in ${directory})` : name;
169:     if (!out.includes(label)) out.push(label);
170:   }
171:   return out;
172: }

174: /** Noun phrases from the task text, used when no subsystem matches. */
175: function componentsFromTerms(task: string): string[] {
176:   const words = splitWords(task).filter((word) => word.length > 3);
177:   const joined = words.join(' ').toLowerCase();
178:   const candidates = [
179:     /([a-z]+) (ownership|eligibility|visibility|availability|permission|access)/g,
180:     /([a-z]+) (service|store|manager|controller|predicate|resolver|registry|panel|dialog|screen|view|model)/g,
181:   ];
182:   const out: string[] = [];
183:   for (const pattern of candidates) {
184:     for (const match of joined.matchAll(pattern)) {
185:       const phrase = `${match[1]} ${match[2]}`.trim();
186:       if (phrase.length > 6 && !out.includes(phrase)) out.push(phrase);
187:     }
188:   }
189:   return out.slice(0, 5);
190: }

205: /** Produce the structured interpretation of a task. Pure and deterministic. */
206: export function interpretTask(input: InterpretTaskInput): TaskInterpretation {
207:   const task = input.task.trim();
208:   const notes: string[] = [];
209:   const affectedFiles = (input.affectedFiles ?? []).map((file) => file.replace(/\\/g, '/').trim()).filter(Boolean);
210: 
211:   const terms = keywords(task);
212:   const identifierTerms = [...new Set(splitWords(task).filter(isIdentifierLike))].map(normalizeTerm);
213: 
214:   const { type, confidence: typeConfidence } = classifyTaskType(task);
215:   const knownSubsystems = [...new Set([...input.config.subsystems, ...input.knownSubsystems])];
216:   const { subsystems, confidence: subsystemConfidence } = inferSubsystems(task, knownSubsystems, terms);
217: 
218:   // Directory names of declared files are trustworthy subsystem hints.
219:   const fileDerivedSubsystems = keywords(affectedFiles.map((file) => file.split('/').slice(0, -1).join(' ')).join(' ')).filter(
220:     (term) => term.length >= 4,
221:   );
222:   let combinedSubsystems = subsystems;
223:   if (fileDerivedSubsystems.length > 0) {
224:     combinedSubsystems = [...new Set([...subsystems, ...fileDerivedSubsystems.filter((term) => term.length > 5)])].slice(0, 4);
225:   }
226: 
227:   const likelyComponents =
228:     affectedFiles.length > 0 ? componentsFromFiles(affectedFiles) : componentsFromTerms(task);
229:   if (affectedFiles.length === 0 && likelyComponents.length === 0) {
230:     notes.push('No affected files supplied and no component names recognised in the task text.');
231:   }
232:   if (subsystems.length === 0) {
233:     if (knownSubsystems.length === 0) {
234:       notes.push('Project memory records no subsystems yet, so subsystem inference is unavailable.');
235:     } else {
236:       notes.push('No stored subsystem name matched the task wording.');
237:     }
238:   }
239: 
240:   const reverseEngineering = isReverseEngineeringTask(task, input.project.phase);
241:   const mode: ContextMode = input.mode && input.mode !== 'auto' ? input.mode : reverseEngineering ? 're' : 'auto';
242: 
243:   const inferredFiles =
244:     affectedFiles.length > 0
245:       ? []
246:       : (input.recentlyChangedFiles ?? [])
247:           .filter((file) => {
248:             const tokens = new Set(pathTokens(file));
249:             return terms.some((term) => tokens.has(term));
250:           })
251:           .slice(0, 8);
252: 
253:   const interpretability: InferenceConfidence =
254:     terms.length === 0 ? 'low' : terms.length < 3 ? 'low' : affectedFiles.length > 0 || combinedSubsystems.length > 0 ? 'high' : 'medium';
255:   if (terms.length < 3) {
256:     notes.push('Short task text: relevance relies mostly on severity, recency and subsystem hints.');
257:   }
258: 
259:   return {
260:     text: task,
261:     taskType: type,
262:     typeConfidence,
263:     subsystems: combinedSubsystems,
264:     subsystemConfidence,
265:     likelyComponents,
266:     affectedFiles,
267:     inferredFiles,
268:     terms,
269:     identifierTerms,
270:     reverseEngineering,
271:     mode,
272:     interpretability,
273:     notes,
274:   };
275: }

277: /** Risk assessment inputs gathered from memory and interpretation. */
278: export interface RiskSignals {
279:   /** True when a critical constraint applies to the matched subsystem. */
280:   hasCriticalConstraint: boolean;
281:   /** Highest-severity open bug touching the task. */
282:   worstOpenBug: Severity | null;
283:   /** Number of stored records that reference the matched subsystem. */
284:   relatedRecordCount: number;
285:   /** True when a previous attempt in this area failed. */
286:   previousFailure: boolean;
287:   /** True when the task type implies broad impact. */
288:   broadTaskType: boolean;
289: }
290: 
291: /** Derive the task risk level and the reasons behind it. */
292: export function assessRisk(signals: RiskSignals): { level: Severity; reasons: string[] } {
293:   const reasons: string[] = [];
294:   let score = 0;
295: 
296:   if (signals.hasCriticalConstraint) {
297:     score += 2;
298:     reasons.push('A critical constraint applies to this subsystem.');
299:   }
300:   if (signals.worstOpenBug === 'critical' || signals.worstOpenBug === 'high') {
301:     score += 2;
302:     reasons.push(`An open ${signals.worstOpenBug}-severity bug affects this area.`);
303:   } else if (signals.worstOpenBug) {
304:     score += 1;
305:     reasons.push('An open bug affects this area.');
306:   }
307:   if (signals.relatedRecordCount >= 5) {
308:     score += 2;
309:     reasons.push('This subsystem is referenced by many stored records, so the logic is reused.');
310:   } else if (signals.relatedRecordCount >= 2) {
311:     score += 1;
312:     reasons.push('This subsystem already has stored engineering history.');
313:   }
314:   if (signals.previousFailure) {
315:     score += 1;
316:     reasons.push('A previous attempt in this area did not succeed.');
317:   }
318:   if (signals.broadTaskType) {
319:     score += 1;
320:     reasons.push('The task type usually implies changed behaviour beyond a single file.');
321:   }
322:   if (reasons.length === 0) reasons.push('No elevated risk signals are recorded for this task.');
323: 
324:   const level: Severity = score >= 4 ? 'critical' : score >= 3 ? 'high' : score >= 1 ? 'medium' : 'low';
325:   return { level, reasons };
326: }

```ts
function verificationSection(brief: Brief): Section {
  const plan = brief.verificationPlan;

}
```

147: function parseFrom<T extends string>(values: readonly T[], raw: unknown): T | undefined {
148:   if (typeof raw !== 'string') return undefined;
149:   const needle = raw.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[\s-]+/g, '_');
150:   return values.find((value) => value.toLowerCase() === needle);
151: }

13: /** A clock frozen at a fixed instant, advanceable by tests. */
14: export function fixedClock(start: string | Date = '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'): Clock & { advance(ms: number): void; set(iso: string): void } {
15:   let current = typeof start === 'string' ? new Date(start) : new Date(start.getTime());
16:   return {
17:     now: () => new Date(current.getTime()),
18:     nowMs: () => current.getTime(),
19:     advance(ms: number) {
20:       current = new Date(current.getTime() + ms);
21:     },
22:     set(iso: string) {
23:       current = new Date(iso);

33: export function parseIso(value: string | null | undefined): Date | null {
34:   if (!value) return null;

39: export function ageInDays(iso: string | null | undefined, clock: Clock): number | null {
40:   const date = parseIso(iso);
41:   if (!date) return null;
42:   return Math.max(0, (clock.nowMs() - date.getTime()) / 86_400_000);
43: }

45: /** Exponential decay with a configurable half-life, in [0, 1]. */
46: export function recencyScore(iso: string | null | undefined, clock: Clock, halfLifeDays: number): number {
47:   const age = ageInDays(iso, clock);
48:   if (age === null) return 0;
49:   if (halfLifeDays <= 0) return 1;
50:   return Math.pow(0.5, age / halfLifeDays);
51: }

53: /** Human-friendly relative age such as "3d ago" or "just now". */
54: export function humanAge(iso: string | null | undefined, clock: Clock): string {

export const TASK_MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.62;

function titleTerms(title: string): Set<string> {
  return new Set(keywords(title));
}

export interface TaskMatch {
  task: Task;
  /** 1 for an exact title match, otherwise a token-overlap ratio. */
  similarity: number;
  /** True when the match is an exact, case-insensitive title comparison. */
  exact: boolean;
}

/**
 * Find the task record a free-text task refers to.
 *
 * Exact title matches win outright. Otherwise the best token overlap among
 * still-open tasks is used, so "Fix technology ownership regression" reuses an
 * existing "Fix the technology ownership regression bug" record instead of
 * creating a duplicate on the second call of the same piece of work.
 */
export function matchTask(tasks: readonly Task[], title: string): TaskMatch | null {
  const needle = title.trim();
  if (needle.length === 0) return null;

  const exact = tasks.find((task) => task.title.trim().toLowerCase() === needle.toLowerCase());
  if (exact) return { task: exact, similarity: 1, exact: true };

  const needleTerms = titleTerms(needle);
  if (needleTerms.size === 0) return null;

  let best: TaskMatch | null = null;
  for (const task of tasks) {
    if (task.status === 'cancelled' || task.status === 'verified_done') continue;
    const similarity = setOverlap(needleTerms, titleTerms(task.title));
    if (similarity < TASK_MATCH_THRESHOLD) continue;
    if (!best || similarity > best.similarity) best = { task, similarity, exact: false };
  }
  return best;
}

/** Normalised input for a single verification claim. */
export interface VerificationClaim {
  method: string;
  command: string | null;
  result: VerificationResult;
  evidence: string[];
}

/** Outcome of classifying a completion's evidence. */
export interface VerificationClassification {
  status: VerificationStatus;
  /** Claims that were accepted, to be stored as verification records. */
  accepted: VerificationClaim[];
  /** Explanations for the caller: what was accepted, downgraded or ignored. */
  notes: string[];
}

/** True when a claim carries something a third party could re-run or re-read. */
export function claimHasEvidence(claim: VerificationClaim): boolean {
  if (claim.result !== 'pass') return false;
  return Boolean(claim.command && claim.command.trim().length > 0) || claim.evidence.length > 0;
}

/**
 * Classify a completion's evidence into a verification status.
 *
 * - `verified`  : at least one passing claim with a command or recorded evidence
 * - `failed`    : at least one claim that reported a failure
 * - `partial`   : claims exist but none are pass-with-evidence
 * - `claimed`   : the agent asserted results without any structured claim
 * - `none`      : nothing was offered
 *
 * `results` is the free-text "what I saw" field; it is deliberately *not*
 * enough for `verified`, because prose is not re-checkable evidence.
 */
export function classifyVerification(input: {
  claims: readonly VerificationClaim[];
  results?: readonly string[];
}): VerificationClassification {
  const notes: string[] = [];
  const accepted = input.claims.filter((claim) => claim.result !== 'unknown' || claim.evidence.length > 0);

  if (input.claims.some((claim) => claim.result === 'fail')) {
    notes.push('At least one verification reported a failure: the task is not verified.');
    return { status: 'failed', accepted, notes };
  }

export interface StatusDecisionInput {
  current: TaskStatus;
  verification: VerificationStatus;
  /** Free-text blockers reported with the completion. */
  blockers: readonly string[];
  /** Explicit status requested by the agent, if any. */
  requested?: TaskStatus | null;
  /** Files the completion says changed; used to detect "nothing changed". */
  filesChanged: number;
}

export interface StatusDecision {
  status: TaskStatus;
  notes: string[];
}

/**
 * Decide the task's status after a work pass.
 *
 * `verified_done` is only reachable with verified evidence — an explicit request
 * for it without evidence is downgraded and reported, which is the single most
 * important rule in this module.
 */
export function decideTaskStatus(input: StatusDecisionInput): StatusDecision {
  const notes: string[] = [];

  if (input.blockers.length > 0) {
    if (input.requested === 'verified_done' || input.requested === 'implementation_done') {
      notes.push(
        `Requested status "${input.requested}" downgraded to "blocked": the completion reported blockers.`,
      );
    }
    return { status: 'blocked', notes };
  }

  if (input.requested) {
    if (input.requested === 'verified_done' && input.verification !== 'verified') {
      notes.push(
        `Requested status "verified_done" was not accepted: verification is "${input.verification}", and ` +
          'verified_done requires a passing command or recorded evidence. Recorded as "implementation_done".',
      );
      return { status: 'implementation_done', notes };
    }
    if (input.requested === 'todo' || input.requested === 'in_progress') {
      notes.push(`Requested status "${input.requested}" honours the explicit request.`);
    }
    return { status: input.requested, notes };
  }

  switch (input.verification) {
    case 'verified':
      return { status: 'verified_done', notes };
    case 'failed':
      notes.push('Implementation is recorded, but verification failed; the task stays open.');
      return { status: 'implementation_done', notes };
    case 'partial':
    case 'claimed':
      notes.push('Implementation recorded; verification is incomplete, so the task is not marked done.');
      return { status: 'implementation_done', notes };
    case 'none':
      if (input.filesChanged === 0 && input.current !== 'todo') {
        notes.push('No files were reported as changed and no verification was given.');
      }
      return { status: 'implementation_done', notes };
  }
}

export function guardConfidence(input: {
  requested: Confidence;
  evidence: readonly string[];
  files: readonly string[];
  symbols: readonly string[];
}): ConfidenceGuardResult {
  const requested = input.requested;
  const hasEvidence = input.evidence.length > 0;
  const hasStaticAnchor = input.files.length > 0 || input.symbols.length > 0 || hasEvidence;

  const cap = (level: Confidence, reason: string): ConfidenceGuardResult => ({
    confidence: level,
    downgradedFrom: requested,
    reason,
  });

  if (confidenceRank(requested) >= confidenceRank('runtime_observed') && !hasEvidence) {
    return cap(
      'statically_supported',
      `${requested} requires recorded runtime evidence; downgraded to statically_supported.`,
    );
  }
  if (confidenceRank(requested) >= confidenceRank('statically_supported') && !hasStaticAnchor) {
    return cap(
      'suspected',
      `${requested} requires at least a file, symbol or evidence reference; downgraded to suspected.`,
    );
  }
  return { confidence: requested, downgradedFrom: null, reason: null };
}

/** One-line description of a stored finding, used in command output. */
export function describeFinding(finding: Finding): string {
  return `${finding.id} [${finding.confidence}] ${truncate(finding.statement, 120)}`;
}

/** One-line description of a stored verification. */
export function describeVerification(verification: Verification): string {
  const command = verification.command ? ` via ${verification.command}` : '';
  return `${verification.id} ${verification.method}${command} → ${verification.result}`;
}

/** True when a task is in a state that still needs work. */
export function needsWork(task: Task): boolean {
  return task.status !== 'verified_done' && task.status !== 'cancelled';
}

export const WEIGHTS = {
  subsystemExact: 0.3,
  subsystemPartial: 0.15,
  files: 0.22,
  terms: 0.2,
  identifiers: 0.12,
  fullText: 0.1,
  severity: 0.1,
  recency: 0.08,
  unresolved: 0.06,
  relationship: 0.15,
  confidence: 0.06,
} as const;

/** Half-life for the recency signal, in days. */
export const RECENCY_HALF_LIFE_DAYS = 45;

/** Items scoring below this are not relevant enough to show. */
export const RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD = 0.16;

export interface RelevanceContext {
  terms: ReadonlySet<string>;
  identifierTerms: ReadonlySet<string>;
  /** Inferred and declared subsystems, best first. */
  subsystems: readonly string[];
  /** Files the task declares or that were inferred. */
  files: readonly string[];
  /** Repository files touched by the most recent commits. */
  recentlyChangedFiles: readonly string[];
  taskType: TaskType;
  /** Id of the task record this call created or matched, if any. */
  taskId: string | null;
  /** Full-text scores by record id (0..1), from `Store.searchMemory`. */
  fullTextScores: ReadonlyMap<string, number>;
  /** Files named by the highest-ranked bug, used as a late tie-breaker. */
  clock: Clock;
}

export interface ScoredItem {
  item: MemoryItem;
  /** Additive score; higher is more relevant. Capped at 1. */
  score: number;
  /** Human-readable explanations, rendered in the brief for transparency. */
  reasons: string[];
  /** Per-signal contributions, kept for tests and diagnostics. */
  breakdown: Record<string, number>;
export function scoreItem(item: MemoryItem, context: RelevanceContext): ScoredItem {
  const breakdown: Record<string, number> = {};
  const reasons: string[] = [];

  const subsystem = subsystemMatch(item.subsystem, context.subsystems);
  if (subsystem.score > 0) {
    breakdown['subsystem'] = subsystem.score;
    reasons.push(`subsystem: ${item.subsystem}`);
  }

  if (context.files.length > 0 && item.files.length > 0) {
    let best = 0;
    let bestFile = '';
    for (const file of item.files) {
      const affinity = bestPathAffinity(file, context.files);
      if (affinity > best) {
        best = affinity;
        bestFile = file;
      }
    }
    if (best > 0) {
      breakdown['files'] = WEIGHTS.files * best;
      reasons.push(best >= 0.8 ? `same file: ${bestFile}` : `related file: ${bestFile}`);
    }
  }

  const itemTerms = new Set(item.terms);
  const coverage = queryCoverage(context.terms, itemTerms);
  if (coverage > 0) {
    breakdown['terms'] = WEIGHTS.terms * coverage;
    if (coverage >= 0.5) reasons.push('matches task wording');
  }

  if (context.identifierTerms.size > 0) {
    let hits = 0;
    const examples: string[] = [];
    for (const identifier of context.identifierTerms) {
      if (itemTerms.has(normalizeTerm(identifier))) {
        hits += 1;
        if (examples.length < 2) examples.push(identifier);
      }
    }
    if (hits > 0) {
      breakdown['identifiers'] = Math.min(1, hits / context.identifierTerms.size) * WEIGHTS.identifiers;
      reasons.push(`mentions ${examples.join(', ')}`);
    }
  }

  const fullText = context.fullTextScores.get(item.id);
  if (fullText && fullText > 0) {
    breakdown['fullText'] = WEIGHTS.fullText * fullText;
  }

  const urgencyScore = urgency(item);
  if (urgencyScore > 0) {
    breakdown['severity'] = WEIGHTS.severity * urgencyScore;
    if (item.kind === 'bug' && item.severity && severityWeight(item.severity) >= severityWeight('high')) {
      reasons.push(`${item.severity}-severity bug`);
    }
    if (item.priority === 'P0' || item.priority === 'P1') reasons.push(`${item.priority} task`);
  }

  const recency = recencyScore(item.createdAt, context.clock, RECENCY_HALF_LIFE_DAYS);
  breakdown['recency'] = WEIGHTS.recency * recency;

  if (isUnresolved(item)) {
    breakdown['unresolved'] = WEIGHTS.unresolved;
  }

  if (context.taskId && item.taskId === context.taskId) {
    breakdown['relationship'] = WEIGHTS.relationship;
    reasons.push('recorded for this task');
  } else if (item.head && item.head.length > 0 && item.kind === 'handoff') {
    // A handoff recorded at a recent HEAD is closer to the current state.
    const matchedFile = context.recentlyChangedFiles.some((file) => item.body.includes(file));
    if (matchedFile) {
      breakdown['relationship'] = WEIGHTS.relationship * 0.5;
      reasons.push('touches files changed in recent commits');
    }
  }

  const confidence = confidenceSignal(item);
  if (confidence > 0) breakdown['confidence'] = WEIGHTS.confidence * confidence;

  const total = Math.min(1, Object.values(breakdown).reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0));
  return { item, score: Number(total.toFixed(4)), reasons, breakdown };
}

export interface ScoreOptions {
  /** Keep only items scoring at least this much. Defaults to RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD. */
  threshold?: number;
  /** Restrict to specific memory kinds. */
  kinds?: readonly MemoryItem['kind'][];
}

/**
 * Score and rank a candidate set.
 *
 * Ordering is fully deterministic: score descending, then a stable tie-break on
 * severity, then creation time descending, then id, so equal scores never
 * reorder between runs.
 */
export function rankItems(
  items: readonly MemoryItem[],
  context: RelevanceContext,
  options: ScoreOptions = {},
): ScoredItem[] {
  const threshold = options.threshold ?? RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD;
  const allowed = options.kinds ? new Set(options.kinds) : null;
  return items
    .filter((item) => (allowed ? allowed.has(item.kind) : true))
    .map((item) => scoreItem(item, context))
    .filter((scored) => scored.score >= threshold)
    .sort((a, b) => {
      if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;
      const severityDelta = (b.item.severity ? severityWeight(b.item.severity) : 0) - (a.item.severity ? severityWeight(a.item.severity) : 0);
      if (severityDelta !== 0) return severityDelta;
      if (a.item.createdAt !== b.item.createdAt) return b.item.createdAt.localeCompare(a.item.createdAt);
      return a.item.id.localeCompare(b.item.id);
    });
}

/** Compact one-line summary of why an item was selected. */
export function reasonSummary(scored: ScoredItem): string {
  return scored.reasons.slice(0, 3).join('; ');
}

/** Resolve a caller-supplied path to an absolute path, following symlinks when it exists. */
export function normalizeUserPath(path: string): string {
  const absolute = resolve(path);
  try {
    return realpathSync(absolute);
  } catch {
    return absolute;
  }

function findProjectByReference(store: Store, reference: string): Project | null {
  const trimmed = reference.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return null;
  return (
    store.getProject(trimmed) ??
    store.getProjectBySlug(slugify(trimmed)) ??
    store.getProjectBySlug(trimmed) ??
    findProjectByName(store, trimmed) ??
    findProjectByFuzzyName(store, trimmed)
  );
}

function findProjectByName(store: Store, name: string): Project | null {
  const needle = name.trim().toLowerCase();
  return store.listProjects().find((project) => project.name.toLowerCase() === needle) ?? null;
}

/** Tolerate near misses such as "concurrent studios" for "concurrent-studios". */
function findProjectByFuzzyName(store: Store, name: string): Project | null {
  const projects = store.listProjects();
  if (projects.length === 0) return null;
  const match = closestMatch(name, projects.map((project) => `${project.slug} ${project.name}`));
  if (!match) return null;
  const matchedSlug = match.split(' ')[0] ?? '';
  return projects.find((project) => project.slug === matchedSlug) ?? null;
}

35: const MIN_TERM_LENGTH = 2;
36: 
37: /**
38:  * Split a string into raw words, breaking camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case,
39:  * kebab-case, dotted and slashed identifiers, plus digit boundaries
40:  * ("F30", "issue42" -> "issue", "42").
41:  */
42: export function splitWords(input: string): string[] {
43:   if (!input) return [];
44:   const out: string[] = [];
45:   for (const chunk of input.split(/[^A-Za-z0-9_]+/)) {
46:     if (!chunk) continue;
47:     for (const part of chunk.split('_')) {
48:       if (!part) continue;
49:       // Break camelCase / PascalCase / letter-digit boundaries.
50:       const pieces = part.match(/[A-Z]+(?![a-z])|[A-Z]?[a-z]+|[0-9]+|[A-Z]/g);
51:       if (pieces) out.push(...pieces);
52:     }
53:   }
54:   return out;
55: }

57: /**
58:  * Lowercase, singularise lightly and drop noise. Used as the canonical form for
59:  * both indexing-time and query-time term matching, so the two always agree.
60:  */
61: export function normalizeTerm(token: string): string {
62:   let t = token.toLowerCase();
63:   if (t.length > 3 && t.endsWith('ies')) t = `${t.slice(0, -3)}y`;
64:   else if (t.length > 3 && t.endsWith('ses')) t = t.slice(0, -2);
65:   else if (t.length > 3 && t.endsWith('s') && !t.endsWith('ss') && !t.endsWith('us')) t = t.slice(0, -1);
66:   return t;
67: }

69: /** Tokenise text into normalised, de-duplicated terms with occurrence counts. */
70: export function termCounts(input: string): Map<string, number> {
71:   const counts = new Map<string, number>();
72:   for (const word of splitWords(input)) {
73:     const term = normalizeTerm(word);
74:     if (term.length < MIN_TERM_LENGTH) continue;
75:     if (STOPWORDS.has(term)) continue;
76:     counts.set(term, (counts.get(term) ?? 0) + 1);
77:   }
78:   return counts;
79: }
80: 
81: /** Normalised unique terms, ordered by first appearance (stable for rendering). */
82: export function keywords(input: string): string[] {
83:   return [...termCounts(input).keys()];
84: }

86: /** True when a term looks like a code identifier rather than prose vocabulary. */
87: export function isIdentifierLike(raw: string): boolean {
88:   return (
89:     /[a-z][A-Z]/.test(raw) ||
90:     raw.includes('_') ||
91:     raw.includes('.') ||
92:     raw.includes('/') ||
93:     raw.includes('()') ||
94:     /^[A-Z]{2,}/.test(raw)
95:   );
96: }

98: /** Split a repository-relative path into meaningful, normalised tokens. */
99: export function pathTokens(path: string): string[] {
100:   const segments = path
101:     .replace(/\\/g, '/')
102:     .split('/')
103:     .flatMap((segment) => {
104:       const dot = segment.lastIndexOf('.');
105:       const base = dot > 0 ? segment.slice(0, dot) : segment;
106:       return splitWords(base);
107:     })
108:     .map(normalizeTerm)
109:     .filter((token) => token.length >= MIN_TERM_LENGTH && !STOPWORDS.has(token));
110:   return [...new Set(segments)];
111: }
112: 
113: /** Directory segments of a path, excluding the basename and generic noise. */
114: function pathSegments(path: string): string[] {
115:   return path
116:     .replace(/\\/g, '/')
117:     .split('/')
118:     .filter(Boolean)
119:     .slice(0, -1)
120:     .map((segment) => normalizeTerm(segment))
121:     .filter((segment) => segment.length >= MIN_TERM_LENGTH && !GENERIC_PATH_SEGMENTS.has(segment));

124: /** Normalise a path for comparison: forward slashes, no leading "./" or trailing "/". */
125: export function normalizePath(path: string): string {
126:   let p = path.replace(/\\/g, '/').trim();
127:   while (p.startsWith('./')) p = p.slice(2);
128:   if (p.length > 1 && p.endsWith('/')) p = p.replace(/\/+$/, '');
129:   return p;

132: function basename(path: string): string {
133:   const normalized = normalizePath(path);
134:   const idx = normalized.lastIndexOf('/');
135:   return idx === -1 ? normalized : normalized.slice(idx + 1);
136: }

138: /**
139:  * Path affinity in [0, 1].
140:  *
141:  * Used to score how strongly a memory record's files relate to the files a task
142:  * touches. Total ordering is: identical path > same basename > shared directory
143:  * segments > shared filename tokens.
144:  */
145: export function pathAffinity(a: string, b: string): number {
146:   if (!a || !b) return 0;
147:   const na = normalizePath(a);
148:   const nb = normalizePath(b);
149:   if (na === nb) return 1;
150: 
151:   // Suffix containment: "src/x/y.ts" vs "y.ts" or "x/y.ts".
152:   if (na.endsWith(`/${nb}`) || nb.endsWith(`/${na}`)) return 0.9;
153: 
154:   const baseA = basename(na);
155:   const baseB = basename(nb);
156:   let score = 0;
157:   if (baseA === baseB) score = 0.8;
158:   else {
159:     const tokensA = new Set(pathTokens(baseA));
160:     const tokensB = new Set(pathTokens(baseB));
161:     if (tokensA.size > 0 && tokensB.size > 0) {
162:       let shared = 0;
163:       for (const token of tokensA) if (tokensB.has(token)) shared += 1;
164:       score = Math.max(score, 0.5 * (shared / Math.max(tokensA.size, tokensB.size)));
165:     }
166:   }
167: 
168:   const dirsA = new Set(pathSegments(na));
169:   const dirsB = new Set(pathSegments(nb));
170:   if (dirsA.size > 0 && dirsB.size > 0) {
171:     let shared = 0;
172:     for (const dir of dirsA) if (dirsB.has(dir)) shared += 1;
173:     if (shared > 0) score = Math.max(score, Math.min(0.55, 0.3 + 0.15 * shared));
174:   }
175:   return Math.min(1, score);
176: }
177: 
178: /** Best affinity between one path and a list of reference paths. */
179: export function bestPathAffinity(path: string, references: readonly string[]): number {
180:   let best = 0;
181:   for (const ref of references) best = Math.max(best, pathAffinity(path, ref));
182:   return best;
183: }

185: /** Overlap of two token sets as a Jaccard-style ratio in [0, 1]. */
186: export function setOverlap<T>(a: ReadonlySet<T>, b: ReadonlySet<T>): number {
187:   if (a.size === 0 || b.size === 0) return 0;
188:   let shared = 0;
189:   for (const item of a) if (b.has(item)) shared += 1;
190:   return shared / (a.size + b.size - shared);
191: }
192: 
193: /**
194:  * Coverage-weighted overlap: how much of the *query* set is covered by the
195:  * candidate. Rewards records that mention many task terms without penalising
196:  * them for being verbose, which Jaccard does.
197:  */
198: export function queryCoverage(query: ReadonlySet<string>, candidate: ReadonlySet<string>): number {
199:   if (query.size === 0 || candidate.size === 0) return 0;
200:   let shared = 0;
201:   for (const term of query) if (candidate.has(term)) shared += 1;
202:   return shared / query.size;
203: }

205: /** Truncate text on a word boundary, appending an ellipsis when cut. */
206: export function truncate(text: string, maxLength: number): string {
207:   const clean = text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
208:   if (clean.length <= maxLength) return clean;
209:   const cut = clean.slice(0, Math.max(0, maxLength - 1));
210:   const space = cut.lastIndexOf(' ');
211:   return `${(space > maxLength * 0.6 ? cut.slice(0, space) : cut).trimEnd()}…`;
212: }

214: /** Cheap token estimate used for budgeting the rendered brief. */
215: export function approxTokens(text: string): number {
216:   return Math.ceil(text.length / 4);
217: }

219: /** Collapse whitespace and strip a trailing period, for list rendering. */
220: export function tidy(text: string | null | undefined): string {
221:   if (!text) return '';
222:   return text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().replace(/\.$/, '');
223: }

225: /** Format a compact bullet list, or an empty string when there is nothing to show. */
226: export function bullets(items: readonly string[]): string {
227:   return items.map((item) => `- ${item}`).join('\n');
228: }

230: /** Case-insensitive substring test that tolerates undefined haystacks. */
231: export function containsIgnoreCase(haystack: string | null | undefined, needle: string): boolean {
232:   if (!haystack || !needle) return false;
233:   return haystack.toLowerCase().includes(needle.toLowerCase());
234: }

236: /** Nearest match from a list of candidates for a free-text term, or undefined. */
237: export function closestMatch(term: string, candidates: readonly string[]): string | undefined {
238:   const needle = normalizeTerm(term);
239:   if (!needle) return undefined;
240:   let best: { value: string; score: number } | undefined;
241:   for (const candidate of candidates) {
242:     const tokens = keywords(candidate);
243:     if (tokens.length === 0) continue;
244:     let score = 0;
245:     for (const token of tokens) {
246:       if (token === needle) score += 1;
247:       else if (token.startsWith(needle) || needle.startsWith(token)) score += 0.5;
248:     }
249:     score /= Math.sqrt(tokens.length);
250:     if (score > 0 && (!best || score > best.score)) best = { value: candidate, score };
251:   }
252:   return best?.value;
253: }

/**
 * Render a bug as a compact, decision-ready line: what is wrong, and how it was
 * observed. Only fields actually recorded are shown.
 */
export function describeBug(bug: Bug): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (bug.observed) parts.push(`observed: ${truncate(bug.observed, 160)}`);
  else if (bug.expected) parts.push(`expected: ${truncate(bug.expected, 120)}`);
  if (bug.reproduction) parts.push(`repro: ${truncate(bug.reproduction, 140)}`);
  return parts.join(' | ');
}

/** Human label for a confidence level, used in reverse-engineering output. */
export function confidenceLabel(confidence: Confidence): string {
  return confidence.replace(/_/g, ' ');
}

```ts
export function section(text: string, title: string): string {
  const lines = text.split('\n');
  const start = lines.findIndex((line) => line === title);
  if (start === -1) return '';
  const rest: string[] = [];
  for (let index = start + 1; index < lines.length; index += 1) {
    const line = lines[index] ?? '';
    // A new section starts at a heading line: non-empty, no leading whitespace,
    // and not a bullet or a numbered item.
    if (line.length > 0 && !/^[\s\-]/.test(line) && !/^\d+\./.test(line) && index > start + 1 && lines[index - 1] === '') break;
    rest.push(line);
  }
  return rest.join('\n');
}
```

```ts
export function section(text: string, title: string): string {
  const lines = text.split('\n');

  if (start === -1) return '';
  const blank = lines.indexOf('', start + 1);
  const end = blank === -1 ? lines.length : blank;

}
```

16:   Verification,
17:   VerificationResult,
18:   VerificationStatus,

23: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
24: // Matching a task string to an existing record
25: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
26: 
27: /** Similarity threshold above which a task string is considered the same task. */
28: export const TASK_MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.62;
29: 
30: function titleTerms(title: string): Set<string> {
31:   return new Set(keywords(title));
32: }
33: 
34: export interface TaskMatch {
35:   task: Task;
36:   /** 1 for an exact title match, otherwise a token-overlap ratio. */
37:   similarity: number;
38:   /** True when the match is an exact, case-insensitive title comparison. */
39:   exact: boolean;
40: }
41: 
42: /**
43:  * Find the task record a free-text task refers to.
44:  *
45:  * Exact title matches win outright. Otherwise the best token overlap among
46:  * still-open tasks is used, so "Fix technology ownership regression" reuses an
47:  * existing "Fix the technology ownership regression bug" record instead of
48:  * creating a duplicate on the second call of the same piece of work.
49:  */
50: export function matchTask(tasks: readonly Task[], title: string): TaskMatch | null {
51:   const needle = title.trim();
52:   if (needle.length === 0) return null;
53: 
54:   const exact = tasks.find((task) => task.title.trim().toLowerCase() === needle.toLowerCase());
55:   if (exact) return { task: exact, similarity: 1, exact: true };
56: 
57:   const needleTerms = titleTerms(needle);
58:   if (needleTerms.size === 0) return null;
59: 
60:   let best: TaskMatch | null = null;
61:   for (const task of tasks) {
62:     if (task.status === 'cancelled' || task.status === 'verified_done') continue;
63:     const similarity = setOverlap(needleTerms, titleTerms(task.title));
64:     if (similarity < TASK_MATCH_THRESHOLD) continue;
65:     if (!best || similarity > best.similarity) best = { task, similarity, exact: false };
66:   }
67:   return best;
68: }

70: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
71: // Verification classification
72: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
73: 
74: /** Normalised input for a single verification claim. */
75: export interface VerificationClaim {
76:   method: string;
77:   command: string | null;
78:   result: VerificationResult;
79:   evidence: string[];
80: }
81: 
82: /** Outcome of classifying a completion's evidence. */
83: export interface VerificationClassification {
84:   status: VerificationStatus;
85:   /** Claims that were accepted, to be stored as verification records. */
86:   accepted: VerificationClaim[];
87:   /** Explanations for the caller: what was accepted, downgraded or ignored. */
88:   notes: string[];
89: }
90: 
91: /** True when a claim carries something a third party could re-run or re-read. */
92: export function claimHasEvidence(claim: VerificationClaim): boolean {
93:   if (claim.result !== 'pass') return false;
94:   return Boolean(claim.command && claim.command.trim().length > 0) || claim.evidence.length > 0;
95: }
96: 
97: /**
98:  * Classify a completion's evidence into a verification status.
99:  *
100:  * - `verified`  : at least one passing claim with a command or recorded evidence
101:  * - `failed`    : at least one claim that reported a failure
102:  * - `partial`   : claims exist but none are pass-with-evidence
103:  * - `claimed`   : the agent asserted results without any structured claim
104:  * - `none`      : nothing was offered
105:  *
106:  * `results` is the free-text "what I saw" field; it is deliberately *not*
107:  * enough for `verified`, because prose is not re-checkable evidence.
108:  */
109: export function classifyVerification(input: {
110:   claims: readonly VerificationClaim[];
111:   results?: readonly string[];
112: }): VerificationClassification {
113:   const notes: string[] = [];
114:   const accepted = input.claims.filter((claim) => claim.result !== 'unknown' || claim.evidence.length > 0);
115: 
116:   if (input.claims.some((claim) => claim.result === 'fail')) {
117:     notes.push('At least one verification reported a failure: the task is not verified.');
118:     return { status: 'failed', accepted, notes };
119:   }
120: 
121:   const evidenced = input.claims.filter(claimHasEvidence);
122:   if (evidenced.length > 0) {
123:     return { status: 'verified', accepted, notes };
124:   }
125: 
126:   if (input.claims.length > 0) {
127:     notes.push(
128:       'Verification claims were recorded without a command or evidence, so they do not count as verified.',
129:     );
130:     return { status: 'partial', accepted, notes };
131:   }
132: 
133:   if ((input.results?.length ?? 0) > 0) {
134:     notes.push(
135:       'Results were described but no test command or evidence was provided: recorded as claimed, not verified.',
136:     );
137:     return { status: 'claimed', accepted: [], notes };
138:   }
139: 
140:   notes.push('No verification evidence was provided: implementation is recorded, verification is missing.');
141:   return { status: 'none', accepted: [], notes };
142: }
143: 
144: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
145: // Task status transitions
146: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
147: 
148: export interface StatusDecisionInput {
149:   current: TaskStatus;
150:   verification: VerificationStatus;
151:   /** Free-text blockers reported with the completion. */
152:   blockers: readonly string[];
153:   /** Explicit status requested by the agent, if any. */
154:   requested?: TaskStatus | null;
155:   /** Files the completion says changed; used to detect "nothing changed". */
156:   filesChanged: number;
157: }
158: 
159: export interface StatusDecision {
160:   status: TaskStatus;
161:   notes: string[];
162: }
163: 
164: /**
165:  * Decide the task's status after a work pass.
166:  *
167:  * `verified_done` is only reachable with verified evidence — an explicit request
168:  * for it without evidence is downgraded and reported, which is the single most
169:  * important rule in this module.
170:  */
171: export function decideTaskStatus(input: StatusDecisionInput): StatusDecision {
172:   const notes: string[] = [];
173: 
174:   if (input.blockers.length > 0) {
175:     if (input.requested === 'verified_done' || input.requested === 'implementation_done') {
176:       notes.push(
177:         `Requested status "${input.requested}" downgraded to "blocked": the completion reported blockers.`,
178:       );
179:     }
180:     return { status: 'blocked', notes };
181:   }
182: 
183:   if (input.requested) {
184:     if (input.requested === 'verified_done' && input.verification !== 'verified') {
185:       notes.push(
186:         `Requested status "verified_done" was not accepted: verification is "${input.verification}", and ` +
187:           'verified_done requires a passing command or recorded evidence. Recorded as "implementation_done".',
188:       );
189:       return { status: 'implementation_done', notes };
190:     }
191:     if (input.requested === 'todo' || input.requested === 'in_progress') {
192:       notes.push(`Requested status "${input.requested}" honours the explicit request.`);
193:     }
194:     return { status: input.requested, notes };
195:   }
196: 
197:   switch (input.verification) {
198:     case 'verified':
199:       return { status: 'verified_done', notes };
200:     case 'failed':
201:       notes.push('Implementation is recorded, but verification failed; the task stays open.');
202:       return { status: 'implementation_done', notes };
203:     case 'partial':
204:     case 'claimed':
205:       notes.push('Implementation recorded; verification is incomplete, so the task is not marked done.');
206:       return { status: 'implementation_done', notes };
207:     case 'none':
208:       if (input.filesChanged === 0 && input.current !== 'todo') {
209:         notes.push('No files were reported as changed and no verification was given.');
210:       }
211:       return { status: 'implementation_done', notes };
212:   }
213: }

215: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
216: // Confidence promotion guard for findings
217: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
218: 
219: export interface ConfidenceGuardResult {
220:   confidence: Confidence;
221:   /** Set when the requested level was reduced. */
222:   downgradedFrom: Confidence | null;
223:   reason: string | null;
224: }
225: 
226: /**
227:  * Keep a finding's confidence honest.
228:  *
229:  * Declaring `runtime_confirmed` requires recorded evidence; declaring
230:  * `statically_supported` or above requires at least a file, symbol or evidence
231:  * reference so the claim is checkable. Requesting more than the input supports
232:  * is downgraded and the reason is reported back.
233:  */
234: export function guardConfidence(input: {
235:   requested: Confidence;
236:   evidence: readonly string[];
237:   files: readonly string[];
238:   symbols: readonly string[];
239: }): ConfidenceGuardResult {
240:   const requested = input.requested;
241:   const hasEvidence = input.evidence.length > 0;
242:   const hasStaticAnchor = input.files.length > 0 || input.symbols.length > 0 || hasEvidence;
243: 
244:   const cap = (level: Confidence, reason: string): ConfidenceGuardResult => ({
245:     confidence: level,
246:     downgradedFrom: requested,
247:     reason,
248:   });
249: 
250:   if (confidenceRank(requested) >= confidenceRank('runtime_observed') && !hasEvidence) {
251:     return cap(
252:       'statically_supported',
253:       `${requested} requires recorded runtime evidence; downgraded to statically_supported.`,
254:     );
255:   }
256:   if (confidenceRank(requested) >= confidenceRank('statically_supported') && !hasStaticAnchor) {
257:     return cap(
258:       'suspected',
259:       `${requested} requires at least a file, symbol or evidence reference; downgraded to suspected.`,
260:     );
261:   }
262:   return { confidence: requested, downgradedFrom: null, reason: null };
263: }

269: /** One-line description of a stored finding, used in command output. */
270: export function describeFinding(finding: Finding): string {
271:   return `${finding.id} [${finding.confidence}] ${truncate(finding.statement, 120)}`;
272: }
273: 
274: /** One-line description of a stored verification. */
275: export function describeVerification(verification: Verification): string {
276:   const command = verification.command ? ` via ${verification.command}` : '';
277:   return `${verification.id} ${verification.method}${command} → ${verification.result}`;
278: }
279: 
280: /** True when a task is in a state that still needs work. */
281: export function needsWork(task: Task): boolean {
282:   return task.status !== 'verified_done' && task.status !== 'cancelled';
283: }

247:   if (!found) {
